text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parliamentarians stage a mass walkout at the National Assembly in an attempt to derail a discussion on the government's financial estimates presented in the 1997/98 budget last week.
- Voter registration is extended to June 30.
- President Daniel arap Moi says parliament is supreme and cannot be sued.
- President Moi says the government has recovered some 384 AK-47 rifles from Pokot area, northwest Kenya, imported to cause chaos in the country.
- A senior Criminal Investigations Department officer is charged with the murder of her husband.
- Vice President George Saitoti says opposition MP's intended to provoke and test the president's tolerance by misbehaving during the budget speech last Thursday.
- The Ministry of Health says it will stress home-based care for AIDS patients to reduce the economic burden on the government following a sharp rise in the number of AIDS patients.
- Students of Langa Langa Secondary school in Nakuru demonstrate over an intended auction of their school land.
